parameter_matrix.note: Synchronous rectification eliminates external Schottky diode loss and PCB area.
Compact WSON/VSON/SOT-563 packages demand tight hot-loop layout and thermal vias.
Verify cold-start minimum startup voltage and bus surge ceiling.
Provides transient overshoot margin above nominal DC supply bus.
Fixed-output variants save divider BOM; adjustable parts allow arbitrary rail tuning.
For boost converters, usable Iout ≈ Isw × (Vin / Vout) × η minus half ripple ΔIL/2.
Dominates light-load efficiency and standby battery runtime.
Higher fsw shrinks inductor footprint; lower fsw reduces switching losses & high-band EMI.
Check datasheet efficiency curve at your exact Vin/Vout/Iout operating point.
Ensure inductor Isat exceeds worst-case peak switch current by >= 20–30%.
Any Vref discrepancy requires recalculating feedback divider R1/R2.
Lower θJA improves continuous load thermal headroom on compact 2-layer PCBs.

swap_risks: CAUTION CURRENT RATING BASIS: TPS61040DBVR specifies 400 mA (switch current limit Isw, p.5) vs TPS61041DBVR 250 mA (switch current limit Isw, p.5). Remember boost Iout,max is strictly less than Isw due to duty-cycle scaling.
BENCH VERIFICATION: Confirm thermal dissipation margin using θJA (TPS61040DBVR: 205.2 °C/W vs TPS61041DBVR: 205.2 °C/W) and worst-case ambient temperature (-40..85 °C vs -40..85 °C).
engineering_verdict: TPS61040DBVR (Texas Instruments, SOT-23-5) and TPS61041DBVR (Texas Instruments, SOT-23-5) are Level 2 Functional / Tuning Required replacements: while the footprint is physically compatible, engineering review and passive/circuit adjustments are mandatory due to current rating or switch-limit basis differs. Key datasheet deltas: topology is boost (non-sync) vs boost (non-sync), switching frequency is 1000 kHz (p.1) vs 1000 kHz (p.4), rated current is 400 mA (p.5) vs 250 mA (p.5), typical inductor is 10 µH (p.4) vs 10 µH (p.4), and Iq is 28 µA (p.5) vs 28 µA (p.5). Always validate pinout orientation (TOP_VIEW p.3 vs TOP_VIEW p.3), thermal margin (θJA 205.2 vs 205.2 °C/W), and official manufacturer datasheets on hardware prototypes before production release.
